question: What is the final recommended timing for a routine post-natal clinical review?
explanation: The final routine post-natal visit occurs at six weeks to evaluate complete physical and psychological recovery. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h1)

question: Why is the first post-natal contact scheduled within the first 24 hours?

options.B: To catch early bleeding and severe neonatal issues

explanation: The initial hours after birth carry the highest risk for life-threatening complications like primary hemorrhage. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h1)

question: What color is lochia serosa during normal postpartum recovery?
explanation: Lochia serosa appears between days four and ten and has a characteristic pinkish-brown coloration. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h2)

question: What does a uterus that remains soft and large after ten days indicate?
explanation: A boggy, uncontracted uterus indicates subinvolution, often caused by retained placental tissue or infection. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h2)

question: A mother cries easily and feels overwhelmed five days after delivery but recovers quickly. What is this condition?
explanation: Postpartum blues are mild, short-lived emotional changes driven by sudden hormonal drops after birth. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h3)

question: What is the normal resting respiratory rate for a healthy newborn?
explanation: A newborn breathes much faster than an adult, with a normal resting range of 30 to 60 breaths per minute. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h4)

question: What immediate action should a nurse take when a newborn's axillary temperature drops to 35.8°C?

options.A: Place the infant under a cold fan for stabilization
options.C: Initiate skin-to-skin contact and wrap the baby warmly
options.D: Begin intravenous fluid resuscitation right away

explanation: Skin-to-skin contact with the mother is the safest and most effective method to reverse mild infant hypothermia. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h4)

question: What is the primary cause of early post-partum hemorrhage?
explanation: Failure of the uterine muscle fibers to contract adequately after delivery is the most common reason for heavy bleeding. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h5)

question: Which clinical sign points most directly toward deep vein thrombosis in a postpartum mother?

options.B: Redness around the perineal repair site
options.C: Unilateral swelling and pain in one calf
options.D: General body weakness and mild dizziness

explanation: Blood clots in deep veins typically obstruct circulation in one leg, causing localized pain, warmth, and swelling. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h5)

question: Why should a postpartum mother wash her perineal area from front to back?

options.A: To speed up the healing of any episiotomy stitches
options.B: To keep the lochia discharge flowing outward
options.C: To prevent the spread of bacteria from the anal region
options.D: To ensure proper blood circulation to the perineum

explanation: Wiping or washing from front to back stops fecal bacteria from contaminating the vaginal and urinary tracts. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h6)

question: What is the primary nutritional goal for a woman who is exclusively breastfeeding?

options.A: Eliminating all dietary fats to prevent infant colic
options.B: Increasing protein, iron, and fluid intake to support milk production
options.C: Taking high-dose vitamin supplements instead of eating meals
options.D: Restricting carbohydrate intake to regain pre-pregnancy weight

explanation: Lactation requires extra energy, protein, and fluids to maintain milk quality and protect the mother's health. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h6)

question: Which contraceptive method is safest for a mother who is exclusively breastfeeding?
explanation: Progestin-only contraceptives do not affect the quality or quantity of breast milk, unlike estrogen-containing options. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h7)

question: What must a nurse emphasize to a breastfeeding mother regarding the return of fertility?

options.A: Breastfeeding offers permanent natural birth control for years
options.B: Ovulation can occur before her menstrual period returns
options.C: Fertility only returns after she stops breastfeeding completely
options.D: Sexual intercourse is unsafe until menses resume normally

explanation: An egg is released before the first postpartum bleed, meaning pregnancy can happen unexpectedly without contraception. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h7)

question: What is the primary role of community health nurses regarding missed post-natal visits?

options.A: Reporting delinquent mothers to local security agencies
options.B: Tracing defaulters to ensure mother and baby receive care
options.C: Providing financial loans for transport to the clinic
options.D: Penalizing families for missing immunization schedules

explanation: Community tracking helps identify vulnerable infants and mothers who missed clinical appointments and brings them back into care. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h8)

question: Why is integrating traditional birth attendants into formal healthcare referral networks important?

options.A: It provides traditional practitioners with formal medical degrees
options.B: It ensures mothers delivering at home still receive timely facility-based follow-up
options.C: It replaces the need for trained midwives in primary health centers
options.D: It stops all home deliveries across rural communities permanently

explanation: Bridging traditional practitioners with formal clinics improves referral rates for complications and routine infant immunizations. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h8)
